#### 1. dystonia 12  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.454)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-936837)

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ATP1A3 that are exclusively associated with one disease and not the other, or demonstration of distinct molecular mechanisms of ATP1A3 dysfunction for each disease. _(variant: rs754733466)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ATP1A3 in these distinct neurological disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets for ion channelopathies affecting neuronal excitability and motor control.

#### 4. cerebellar ataxia-areflexia-pes cavus-optic atrophy-sensorineural hearing loss syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.417)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-936837)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP8A2 (HGNC:24758) —DISRUPTS→ Plasma membrane calcium-transporting ATPase activity (GO:0005387); ATP1A3 (HGNC:617) —DISRUPTS→ Na+/K+-ATPase activity (GO:0005384); Na+/K+-ATPase activity (GO:0005384) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar ataxia (HP:0001251); Na+/K+-ATPase activity (GO:0005384) —LEADS_TO→ Areflexia (HP:0001297); Plasma membrane calcium-transporting ATPase activity (GO:0005387) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000365); Plasma membrane calcium-transporting ATPase activity (GO:0005387) —LEADS_TO→ Optic atrophy (HP:0000647); Plasma membrane calcium-transporting ATPase activity (GO:0005387) —LEADS_TO→ Pes cavus (HP:0001787). Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in ATP1A3 disrupt Na+/K+-ATPase activity, contributing to cerebellar ataxia and areflexia. Both disrupted ion transport pathways converge on cellular dysfunction in neuronal and sensory tissues, manifesting the overlapping clinical features.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that pathogenic variants in ATP8A2 and ATP1A3 do not lead to loss-of-function or that the affected pathways (Na+/K+-ATPase and Ca2+-ATPase activity) are not critical for neuronal and sensory cell integrity. _(variant: Presence of common benign variants in the coding regions of ATP8A2 and ATP1A3 in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic basis involving fundamental ion transport mechanisms could enable the development of targeted therapies for both diseases, potentially by modulating ion homeostasis or downstream cellular signaling pathways affected by altered ion gradients.
